newsitem.title: USA: Snow brings Nebraska wheat much-needed moisture.
newsitem.headline: Snow brings Nebraska wheat much-needed moisture.

text.p: A late winter storm over the weekend brought blizzard conditions and much-needed moisture to Nebraska's wheat crop, according to a crop condition report from the State Agricultural Statistics Service.

"The much-needed moisture will benefit the western wheat crop and newly seeded oats, but raised concerns about flooding along the Missouri River considering the heavy snows in the Dakotas this winter," the report said.
The wheat crop was rated six percent poor, 39 percent fair, 49 percent good and six percent excellent as of April 6.
As of Sunday, 36 percent of the oat crop had been seeded. This compared to 22 percent last year and 30 percent for the five-year average, the report said.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent very short, 26 percent short, 68 percent adequate and five percent surplus.

Corn planting had not yet begun in most areas of the state due to cool soil temperatures. Producer activities early in the week included oats seeding, spring tillage, stalk shredding, fertilizer application and livestock care, the report said.
